'''Tongseng''' is an [[Indonesian cuisine|Indonesian]] [[goat meat]],<ref>{{cite book | title=Traditional Dietary Culture Of S | publisher=Taylor & Francis | year=2013 | isbn=978-1-136-88794-9 | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=4Un8AQAAQBAJ&pg=PA351 | ref={{sfnref | Taylor & Francis | 2013}} | access-date=January 30, 2015}}</ref> [[Lamb and mutton|mutton]]<ref name="Lexus">{{cite book | author=Lexus | title=Indonesian: A Rough Guide Phrasebook | publisher=Rough Guides | year=1997 | isbn=978-1-85828-250-3 | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=TQhHi1XFMjIC&pg=PA186 | access-date=January 30, 2015 | page=186}}</ref> or [[beef]] stew dish in curry-like soup, with vegetables and ''[[kecap manis]]'' (sweet soy sauce). ''Tongseng'' is commonly found in the [[Indonesia]]n region of [[Central Java]]; from [[Surakarta]] to [[Yogyakarta]]. However, it is believed that the dish originated from Klego district in [[Boyolali Regency|Boyolali]], Central Java.<ref name="CNN-Tongseng">{{cite news | title = Sepotong Sejarah Autentik Indonesia dalam Semangkuk Tongseng | author = Christina Andhika Setyanti | date = 30 August 2016 | work = CNN Indonesia | language = id | url = http://www.cnnindonesia.com/gaya-hidup/20160830160605-262-154892/sepotong-sejarah-autentik-indonesia-dalam-semangkuk-tongseng/}}</ref>
